nodes.description: Private uint16 constant-like state variable (16595) used as a threshold and part of the modulo bound for the pseudo-random decision.
Private uint16 state variable (12587) used together with FREE_WILL as the modulo bound for the pseudo-random decision.
State variable holding a reference to the external IReflectionsDataChannel contract at a hard-coded address; used for outbound calls.
Public address state variable set in the constructor and used as the sole access-control principal.
Constructor that initializes owner with msg.sender.
Owner-restricted function that derives a pseudo-random value from block data and calls the external channel to post a message and update the owner.
Owner-restricted backup function that calls the external channel to set the owner back to the stored owner address.
Caller-controlled address used for access control and mixed into the pseudo-randomness.
Miner/validator-influenced timestamp mixed into the pseudo-randomness seed.
Local uint256 computed from blockhash, coinbase, difficulty, timestamp and msg.sender, reduced modulo (FREE_WILL + FATE).
External call to the untrusted channel contract posting a decision message.
External call to the untrusted channel contract updating the reflected owner from within decide().
External call to the untrusted channel contract updating the reflected owner from within restoreOwner().

edges.reason: Constructor assigns the owner state variable directly from the caller-controlled msg.sender.
decide() gates execution with require(msg.sender == owner), making the caller the access-control subject.
The owner state variable is read to authorize the caller inside decide().
block.timestamp is hashed into the random local variable, making the outcome timestamp dependent.
msg.sender is hashed into the random local variable as part of the pseudo-random seed.
FREE_WILL participates in the modulo bound (FREE_WILL + FATE) applied to the hash.
FATE participates in the modulo bound (FREE_WILL + FATE) applied to the hash.
The comparison random < FREE_WILL selects the branch executed inside decide().
The random local variable feeds the branch selection and the emitted Decided event in decide().
The channel state variable is the target receiver of the postMessage external call.
The random-based branch determines which message string is passed to channel.postMessage.
The channel state variable is the target receiver of the updateOwner external call in decide().
The channel state variable is the target receiver of the updateOwner external call in restoreOwner().
The owner state variable is passed as the argument to channel.updateOwner inside decide().
restoreOwner() gates execution with require(msg.sender == owner), making the caller the access-control subject.
The owner state variable is read to authorize the caller inside restoreOwner().
The external call channel.postMessage hands control to an untrusted contract before decide() completes, allowing reentrant callbacks.
The external call channel.updateOwner inside decide() transfers control to an untrusted contract, enabling reentrancy.
The external call channel.updateOwner inside restoreOwner() transfers control to an untrusted contract, enabling reentrancy.

normalization_plan.reason: The non-core local variable random is only produced and consumed inside decide(); its dataflow contribution is folded into the decide() core function node.
